cells.text: The pain, bleeding, hematoma, swelling of the joint and infection of the incision after treatment with acupotomy (4/1)
Acupotomy is a safe and effective treatment for KOA. Acupotomy’s potential for KOA treatment in alleviating knee pain or related symptoms for short-term and long-term.
Acupuncture, electroacupuncture, sodium hyaluronate (not reported) radiofrequency electrotherapy and NSAIDs (1–5 wk/not reported)
Acupotomy therapy may be effective in reducing pain and improving the physical function of individuals with KOA.
Pain, palpitations, and increased blood pressure (3/1)
Acupotomy may be an effective and safe treatment for KOA.
Acupotomy combined with acupuncture and moxibustion
Other treatment methods other than acupotomy
Acupotomy combined with acupuncture and moxibustion for KOA can increase treatment efficiency and relieve postoperative pain.
Acupotomy efficient than acupuncture for the treatment of KOA.

Acupotomy combined with maneuver in the treatment of KOA has significant curative effect, which can more effectively reduce the degree of knee pain, improve the function of knee joint, and is relatively safe under the standard operation.
Other treatments other than acupotomy combined with massage (not reported)
Acupotomy combined with massage has a significant clinical effect in the treatment of KOA.
Acupotomy has certain advantages in improving clinical symptoms of KOA, protecting the knee cartilage, recovering the knee function.
Acupotomy therapy is an effective method for the treatment of KOA, and its curative effect is better than that of acupuncture.
